clue.text: Harrow boarding school fixture last to come back

parts.note: a bed is a standard fitting in a boarding school dormitory

indicators.note: coming back means the word for last is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: to last is to live on, to survive

explanation.surface: A school sports fixture involving Harrow, a famous English boarding school, is the last one to return.
explanation.walkthrough: Harrow looks like the public school, but here it is the verb meaning to distress, and 'boarding school fixture' is furniture, not a match.
explanation.definitionFit: To harrow someone is to torment or trouble them, which is what bedevil means.

clue.text: Pro during sporting activity getting skimmed dairy product

indicators.note: during says the word for pro sits within the shortened game
skimming takes off the top, so the first letter of the game goes

parts.note: croquet is a lawn game played with mallets and balls
pro means in favour of, for

explanation.surface: A professional at some sport is given skimmed milk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skimmed dairy product' reads as skimmed milk, but skimmed belongs to the wordplay: skimming removes the top of the game's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Roquefort is a French blue cheese made from ewe's milk, so a dairy product.

clue.text: Flag new soldiers raised amid extremes of emotion

indicators.note: amid says these letters go between the two outer letters of emotion
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: its outer letters are taken

indicators.note: in a down clue raising a word turns it upwards, so it is read backwards

parts.note: GIs are American soldiers

explanation.surface: A flag is raised among new recruits in an emotional ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'raised' means written upwards, so the soldiers are read bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: An ensign is a flag, especially one flown by a ship to show its nationality.

clue.text: Next spinner ending in India after a bit of money

indicators.note: after places the DJ and the letter from India behind the A

parts.note: a DJ, disc jockey, spins records

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its last letter

parts.note: its last letter is taken
a cent is a small coin, one hundredth of a dollar

explanation.surface: A spinning bowler finishes his tour of India after earning a bit of money.
explanation.walkthrough: Spinner suggests a cricket bowler, but it is the record-spinning disc jockey; 'after a' sets the A at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjacent means lying next to or beside something, a close synonym for next.

clue.text: Writer's famous expression graduate defined well

parts.note: A-list describes the most famous celebrities
an air is a manner or look, an expression on the face
MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate
clean lines or a clean edge are crisply defined

explanation.surface: A writer's well-known saying is something a graduate defined precisely.
explanation.walkthrough: A-LIST (famous) and AIR (expression) make ALISTAIR; MA and CLEAN give the surname. 'Writer's' has 's standing for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Alistair MacLean was a Scottish novelist famous for thrillers like The Guns of Navarone and Where Eagles Dare.

clue.text: Sprawling lounge cherished by Dallas tycoon who entertains

indicators.note: being cherished is being held close, so the rearranged letters sit inside the tycoon's initials

parts.note: J.R. Ewing was the oil tycoon in the TV soap Dallas

indicators.note: sprawling suggests something spread untidily, so the letters of lounge are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A sprawling lounge is the pride of a Dallas oil tycoon who loves hosting.
explanation.walkthrough: Dallas was a US TV soap whose villain J.R. Ewing supplies the initials.
explanation.definitionFit: A jongleur was a medieval travelling minstrel or juggler who performed for audiences.

clue.text: Soldier caught during hundred year conflict here

indicators.note: during places the soldier and caught inside the hundred and year letters

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
RE, the Royal Engineers, stands for a soldier
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A soldier was captured in the course of the Hundred Years' War.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like the Hundred Years' War itself; 'hundred' and 'year' just supply C and Y, with REC put between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Crécy in northern France was the site of the English victory of 1346, an early battle of the Hundred Years' War.

clue.text: Boxer's first down in fight after agreement, most likely

indicators.note: after says the altered fight follows the agreement

parts.note: a nod signals agreement

indicators.note: in a down clue going down means moving further along, so the letter shifts later in the word

parts.note: a bout is a fight, especially in boxing

indicators.note: a word's first means its first letter

parts.note: its first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A boxer goes down first in a bout after a deal, as is most likely in a fixed fight.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'down' means lower in the column, so the boxer's initial slides to the end of the fight.
explanation.definitionFit: No doubt is an idiom meaning probably or certainly, so most likely.

clue.text: Pity one couldn't fly into Nevis, say

indicators.note: into puts the bird inside the mountain word

parts.note: Ben Nevis is the highest mountain in Britain, so Ben is a mountain
the moa was a huge flightless bird of New Zealand

explanation.surface: Pity the person who couldn't fly to the Caribbean island of Nevis.
explanation.walkthrough: Nevis looks like the island, but 'say' points to Ben Nevis: BEN is a Scottish word for a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: To bemoan is to lament or express sorrow over, close to the verb pity.

clue.text: Pub quiz's second part done using cunning hint

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: the second part of the word is its second letter

parts.note: its second letter is taken

indicators.note: cunning suggests craft and contrivance, so the letters of done are reworked

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: At the pub quiz, the second round is completed with the help of a crafty hint.
explanation.walkthrough: INN and U (second letter of quiz) start the answer; 'cunning' turns DONE into ENDO.
explanation.definitionFit: An innuendo is an indirect, suggestive remark, a sly insinuation.

clue.text: Vehicle inside I've sprayed, going with American smoker?

indicators.note: inside puts the vehicle within the rearranged letters
sprayed suggests scattering, so the letters of I've are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder
an SUV is a sport utility vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone has spray-painted a car with an American who smokes sitting inside.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the smoker is not a person but a mountain that emits smoke.
explanation.definitionFit: Vesuvius is the active volcano above Naples, and a volcano that puffs out smoke is a whimsical smoker.

clue.text: Display loafer, type in navy discounted

indicators.note: discounted means left out, so the sailor's letters are removed

parts.note: a layabout is an idle person, a loafer
an AB, able seaman, is a sailor in the navy

explanation.surface: A shop displays a loafer-style shoe, a navy type, at a discount.
explanation.walkthrough: Loafer suggests a shoe, but it is an idle person, LAYABOUT; removing AB leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A layout is the arrangement or display of material on a page or in a space.

clue.text: Orchestra wrong, sounding increasingly unreal

parts.note: a sin is a wrong

indicators.note: sounding says the word is said aloud and spelt as heard

parts.note: phonier means more fake, comparative of phony

explanation.surface: The orchestra played wrong notes, sounding ever less real.
explanation.walkthrough: PHONIER said without the final R sounds like FONIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinfonia is a symphony, and the name is used by small orchestras such as chamber ensembles.

clue.text: Hot and sunny periodically, leading to fruit deluge

indicators.note: leading to says the fruit comes next

parts.note: hot means fashionable, which is in

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so every other letter of sunny is taken

parts.note: its alternate letters are taken
a date is a fruit

explanation.surface: Hot and sunny weather at times leads to a flood of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: IN (hot, as in fashionable), then UN from alternate letters of 'sunny' picked by 'periodically', then DATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To inundate is to flood or swamp, so to deluge.

clue.text: Georgia's here promoting career, revealed husband

indicators.note: promoting moves upward, and in a down clue that reads the word backwards

parts.note: to career is to rush along; speed
out means revealed or exposed

explanation.surface: In Georgia a woman pushing her career has revealed her husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'promoting' turns SPEED upward to DEEPS in this down clue, then OUT and H.
explanation.definitionFit: The Deep South is the region of the southern US that includes the state of Georgia.

clue.text: Appoint and employ nurses together

indicators.note: nurses means holds or cradles, so the words contain the answer

explanation.surface: A hospital appoints and employs nurses as a team.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through appoINT AND EMploy; 'nurses' looks like the people being hired, but it is the verb meaning holds.
explanation.definitionFit: In tandem is an idiom for side by side or jointly, from the bicycle built for two.

clue.text: Dense element muscle in disturbing cat mainly

indicators.note: disturbing suggests breaking into, so the muscle and in go inside the cat
mainly means most of it, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a puma is a big cat
lats are the latissimus dorsi muscles of the back

explanation.surface: A heavy element pulls a muscle while disturbing a cat.
explanation.walkthrough: The cat is a big cat, the puma, and 'mainly' drops its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Platinum is a precious metal and one of the densest of all chemical elements.

clue.text: Trope of two different books on tablets

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so the books come before the tablets

parts.note: two kinds of books: LIT, short for literature, and OT, the Old Testament
Es are ecstasy tablets

explanation.surface: A figure of speech found in two different books written on stone tablets.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'two different books' give LIT (literature) and OT (Old Testament), sitting on ES.
explanation.definitionFit: Litotes is a figure of speech using understatement, as in 'not bad' for good.

clue.text: Shrewd stocking bananas (only kilo left)

indicators.note: bananas means crazy, so the letters of stocking are rearranged
left means gone away, so the K is taken out of the fodder

explanation.surface: A shrewd shopper stocks up on bananas, with only a kilo left on the shelf.
explanation.walkthrough: Take K out of STOCKING and rearrange the rest; 'stocking' is not a sock here but the letters to shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnostic means relating to knowledge, and so knowing or wise in an older sense.

clue.text: Heavy beat pervades single

indicators.note: pervades means spreads through, so the word for beat goes inside

parts.note: alone means single, on one's own
to cap is to beat or outdo

explanation.surface: A heavy beat runs through a single, as in a hit record.
explanation.walkthrough: Heavy reads as an adjective for music, but here it is a gangster's thug; beat and single are not musical either.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy is slang for a tough or criminal thug, and Al Capone was the most notorious Chicago gangster.

clue.text: Particular clock with a screw loose

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a ... clock, a specific type of clock with a bird that pops out

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a faulty clock; the second phrase is in fact the idiom for being slightly mad.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a kind of chiming clock and is also informal for someone eccentric or crazy.

clue.text: Son bitter about A levels

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word for bitter is read backwards

parts.note: tart means sharp or bitter

explanation.surface: A son is bitter about his A-level results.
explanation.walkthrough: A levels reads as the exams, but A is just a letter and levels the definition. 'about' turns TART into TRAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Strata are layers of rock or society, and so levels.

clue.text: Woman's sponge cake, not mine, splitting

indicators.note: not says the letters of mine are taken out
splitting says the letters of mine come out separately from different places

parts.note: a madeleine is a small French sponge cake

explanation.surface: A woman's sponge cake is split, but not by me.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove M, I, N and E from MADELEINE one by one, as 'splitting' allows, and ADELE is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Adele is a female first name, as borne by the singer, so it stands for a woman.

clue.text: Game pair finishing puzzle outside like this clue

indicators.note: outside means the two letters wrap around the word for this clue
the pair finishing a word is its last two letters

parts.note: its last two letters are taken
this is an across clue

explanation.surface: A pair of solvers finishing a puzzle together, with this clue outstanding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like this clue' refers to the clue itself: it is 23 Across, so ACROSS. L and E, the last two letters of 'puzzle', go around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacrosse is a team game played with netted sticks.

clue.text: Person turning up curtains for student in PM once

indicators.note: for says the end replaces the student letter

parts.note: Clement Attlee was British Prime Minister from 1945 to 1951
L is a learner, a student driver
curtains means the end

explanation.surface: Curtains for the student at the former Prime Minister's party.
explanation.walkthrough: In ATTLEE, the L (learner, a student) is swapped for END.
explanation.definitionFit: An attendee is someone present at an event, someone who turns up.

clue.text: Be more smart in France or Turkey

parts.note: ou is the French for or
a turkey is a fool, a twit

explanation.surface: Showing who is smarter in France or in Turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: Turkey and France look like countries; turkey here is the foolish person, and the French word for or gives OU.
explanation.definitionFit: To outwit someone is to beat them by being cleverer.

clue.text: Male possibly in Mensa? Unlikely

indicators.note: in places the sex inside the rearranged letters
unlikely suggests things are out of their usual order, so the letters of Mensa are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder
male is one example of a sex

explanation.surface: A man who might belong to Mensa, the high-IQ society? Hardly.
explanation.walkthrough: Essex Man is the British stereotype of a brash, materialistic working-class Tory voter from the county east of London, hardly a Mensa type.
explanation.definitionFit: The stereotype is mocked as unintellectual, so membership of a society for the very clever is unlikely.
